PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds revealed in
earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only tells you how often this line type was paid at all.
- If you decide the line is indemnified and no cap, sub-limit or percentage reduction applies,
  take the stated amount as t and give a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. These
  amounts are before such policy arithmetic; apply caps and reductions on top.
- A line type that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies
  do not carry; price it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.
- line 5 "Grub screw": indemnified in the one earlier case; when indemnified t per pc about 1.10 (80% range 0.79 to 1.71); revealed per pc: 0.90-1.30 (case 40), so this line (8 pc) about 8.8 (6.3 to 13.6)
- line 7 "Two-screw pipe clamp 25 mm": indemnified in the one earlier case; when indemnified t per pc about 6.2 (80% range 4.6 to 9.4); revealed per pc: >=5.7 (case 40), so this line (4 pc) about 25 (18.3 to 38)
- line 8 "Service technician hours": indemnified in all 4 earlier cases; when indemnified t per hr about 88 (80% range 72 to 104); revealed per hr: 44-49 (case 21), >=81 (case 39), >=81 (case 39), >=88 (case 40), so this line (6.75 hr) about 595 (485 to 702)
- line 9 "Helper hours": indemnified in the one earlier case; when indemnified t per hr about 73 (80% range 55 to 101); revealed per hr: >=67 (case 40), so this line (5.75 hr) about 418 (316 to 581)
- line 11 "Binding wire": indemnified in the one earlier case; when indemnified t per kg about 9.8 (80% range 7.2 to 15.0); revealed per kg: >=9.0 (case 40), so this line (2 kg) about 19.6 (14.5 to 30)
- line 14 "Small parts and consumables": indemnified in the one earlier case; when indemnified t per pc about 36 (80% range 27 to 55); revealed per pc: >=33 (case 40)
- line 15 "Vehicle costs": indemnified in 14 of 29 earlier cases, t = 0 in 15; when indemnified t per pc about 79 (80% range 72 to 87); revealed per pc: >=76 (case 21), >=74 (case 27), >=83 (case 34), >=76 (case 34), >=65 (case 39), >=71 (case 40)
- line 16 "Construction waste disposal": indemnified in all 2 earlier cases; when indemnified t per pc about 60 (80% range 51 to 71); revealed per pc: >=57 (case 18), 58-61 (case 40)
- line 17 "Processing flat fee": NOT indemnified (t = 0) in all 9 earlier cases; no price evidence

items.rationale: Sections 2.4.3(a), 7.1.5 and 7.1.9 cover the pipe needed to repair the failed joint at plain-copper rates, not the chrome premium or the full 6.4 m without evidence it was needed. Allow about 1 m at €15 gross.
Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.9 limit payment to standard fittings needed for the local repair. Allow two ordinary elbows at about €10 each if this was the size used to reconnect the failed section.

Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.8(e) require a documented connection to the failed joint, which is not established for the five 28 mm elbows. If one was needed, §7.1.9 limits it to about €20 for a standard copper elbow.
The 45° elbow is not shown to be necessary for the joint repair under §§7.1.5 and 7.1.8(e). If substantiated, §7.1.9 caps it at about €20 for one ordinary copper elbow.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers minor fasteners used in the repair. At the Case 40 rate of €1.10 each, four screws allocated to the local repair total €4.40.
The 10 mm size does not match the documented 15 mm replacement pipe, so §7.1.8(e) weighs against payment. If a repair use is substantiated, allow about €5 for one clamp.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers supports needed for reinstatement, but §7.1.8(e) requires that the size suit the repaired installation. If verified, allow two clamps at the reference rate of €6.20 each.
Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(g) cover labour for the failed joint, not time installing the upgrades and new devices. Allow about 2.5 hours for isolation, repair and testing at €88 gross per hour.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers necessary trade labour only; 5.75 helper hours are not justified for a single joint. If assistance was needed for the local repair, allow about one hour at €73.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9 allow the cost of replacing disturbed insulation with ordinary rock wool, not the Armaflex premium. Allow two shells at about €20 each for the local repair.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers ordinary consumables attributable to reinsulating the repair, but §7.1.8(e) does not support 2 kg for one joint. At €9.80/kg, a local allowance of about 0.25 kg is €2.45.
Section 7.1.9 excludes installations that were not present before the loss; the sensor is a new addition, not reinstatement.
Section 7.1.9 excludes the mixing valve because there was no pre-loss valve to replace.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.8(e) allow legitimate repair consumables even when billed as a lump sum. Allow €20 for the single-joint repair, below Case 40's €36 allowance for a broader repair.
Section 7.1.7(f) allows the first travel charge for this contractor's invoice. The comparable gross allowance is €79.
Sections 5.2.1 and 7.1.7(a) cover disposal of material removed for the insured repair, not waste from the elective upgrades. Allow €35 for the small quantity from the joint and its insulation.
Section 7.1.8(b) expressly excludes processing charges levied in addition to itemised labour and materials.
